observation.visible_scene: A dance studio with white walls, a dark ceiling with track lights and an air-conditioning unit, and a full-height mirror wall on the right. A single woman is seen from behind, standing near the mirror; her front is visible as her mirror reflection (not a second person). She wears a gray tank top, a yellow wrap skirt tied at the waist, yellow leg warmers and white sneakers, with dark hair in a ponytail and a side braid. The framing and background stay fixed across all frames, indicating a stationary camera.
visible_changes: At the start (t=0.00–0.12) her arms are raised to about shoulder/head height with open hands, mirrored in the reflection; both feet are planted.
From t=0.16 to t=0.24 she lowers her arms, folding them across her chest and then letting them drop toward her waist; the reflection shows the same descent.

From about t=0.24 onward she lifts one foot behind her with the knee bent (heel toward the calf/buttock), while the other foot stays on the floor; this bent-leg posture is held through the rest of the clip.
The raised foot and skirt hem show small positional shifts between consecutive frames, consistent with a light rhythmic bounce or kick-behind rather than a fully frozen pose.
From about t=0.80 onward she places both hands on her hips, holding this arm position while the bent-leg posture continues to the last frame (t=1.60).
The mirror reflection reproduces each of these body changes in left-right flipped form throughout.
outside_clip_unknowns: The beginning and end of the dance phrase (the arms are already raised at the crop start and the routine is still in progress at the crop end).
Any footwork or leg side-switch that may occur outside this window.
The accompanying music or the name of the choreography.
uncertain_details: Whether the bent leg stays on the same side the whole time or alternates; the small frame-to-frame shifts could be a bounce rhythm or a slow leg change.
Whether the initial raised-hand gesture is a clap, a wave, or a held pose.
The exact height and timing of the leg lift are hard to resolve at 25 fps.
Minor skirt flutter is motion-induced deformation, not a separate object.
